title: Docs: revise section on configuration
body:
Update description and examples of how to write the configfile.

Closes: https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/issues/1278

# Checklist

- [ ] I am familiar with [ASE's contribution guidelines](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/contribute.html).
- [ ] [**Doc strings**](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/python_codingstandard.html#writing-documentation-in-the-code) in code changed in this MR are up to date.
- [ ] [**Unit tests** have been added for new or changed code.](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/tests.html)
- [ ] [**Issue is resolved** via "closes #XXXX" if applicable.](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/user/project/issues/managing_issues.html#closing-issues-automatically)
author: askhl

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body: We should probably just use `python` as the command and not `python3`. I don't even have `python3` as a command on my machine. Doing `python3` on my Windows machine opens the Windows Store to install Python...

comments.body:
Note: I'm not referring to the green highlighted part that Gitlab chose to highlight.

While we're on it, I'm not sure that the "Calculator keywords" section starting on line 219 is helpful for end-users really. It might be worth removing altogether.

comments.author: askhl
comments.body: I opted to remove it since it is very outdated.  It would be good to take a fresh look at kpts and perhaps smearing keywords, their behaviours and how they are documented.

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body:
Most users are not really familiar with class inheritance, so it might be worth mentioning that `BaseProfile` exists and that all calculators take those arguments in addition to the calculator-specific ones, hyperlinking to that base class.

We should also provide a concrete example. For instance, here, `command` is never actually defined (it is mentioned above in a configuration file, but that's different). For the example, we should have a code block that looks something like

```
command = "whatever the command is" #<-- fix this of course lol
profile = AbinitProfile(command=command)
calc = Abinit(profile=profile)
```

comments.author: AndrewRosen
comments.body:
Thanks! This is looking great so far. A few other suggestions while we're on it:

For this MR:

- It might be worthwhile to break the "Calculator configuration" section into multiple distinct subsections with different headers for ease of viewing. I'd suggest "Configuration file", "Environment variable" (for this, we should provide a specific example), and "Profile instantiation".

For this or future MRs:

- The ["Adding new calculators" section](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/calculators.html) still refers to `FileIOCalculator` instead of `GenericFileIOCalculator` and should be updated.
- In the [ORCA docs](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/ase/calculators/orca.html#setup-and-usage), we should probably change `OrcaProfile(["/full/path/to/my/orca"])` such that it explicitly calls `command=` in `OrcaProfile`. This is both because it's best practice to call keyword arguments by their names and because if we add a new argument to `OrcaProfile` one day, it won't break things.
- There are likely a bunch of other individual calculator pages that will need updating. For instance, the "Parallelism" section of the [Espresso docs](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/ase/calculators/espresso.html#parallelism) are now outdated. cc @tomdemeyere.
- In line with the above, a search of "parallel_info" pulls up a few items that will certainly need updating: https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/search.html?q=parallel_info&check_keywords=yes&area=default
- At some point, we will probably want to add a developer page called "Designing a custom calculator" that outlines how to make a custom `GenericFileIOCalculator`. This page should also emphasize that `GenericFileIOCalculator` is the currently recommended standard (at least for IO based calculators). Most users and even developers don't have a clue about `GenericFileIOCalculator` and continue to use old, outdated classes. Discussed in https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/issues/1278.
